protocol.name: cupertino_transaction_v1

description.summary: changes of several components that the server starts on one frame, and holes for windows

protocol.description:
A transaction groups changes of one or more participants and starts them on the same presented frame. A participant is a connection of a shell component; the server takes part with the window changes a participant asks of it. The changes themselves are described with the protocols that carry them already: a surface's content and the values, animations and looks of its layers and its presentation (cupertino_layers_v1) travel in the surface's commit, and a window change is a request on a role object. A transaction holds those commits and requests back and applies them together. Motion is never streamed: an animation is a target with the parameters of a timed curve or a spring, which the server evaluates on the clock of the transaction's output with the functions the toolkit evaluates.
A transaction may be bound to a touchpad gesture the server recognises: the gesture's progress then stands in for time, and the release settles the transaction along a spring with the gesture's velocity, with no message between the processes while the fingers move.
A hole is a layer of a component's surface in which the server draws a window, a minimized window's picture or a workspace, moving, scaling, fading and clipped with that layer.
The protocol is private: the server and the hosts are built from one source. Every change of a message raises the version of its interface, and a message added after version 1 carries the version that added it. A host binds an interface only at the version it was built with (cupertino_host_v1).

interface.name: cupertino_transaction_manager_v1

description.summary: makes transactions and holes

interface.description:
Global singleton, offered only on a connection the server handed out for a component (cupertino_host_component_v1.connection). A transaction is named by the component that created it, the instance number of that component's connection (cupertino_component_v1.component) and a serial that instance chose, so the creator tells another component the name without waiting for the server, and the names of a restarted component never meet the names of the instance before.
A connection takes part in at most 16 transactions that have not ended, the ones it created and the ones it joined counted together.
Version 2 ends every transaction and says so: a transaction no gesture drives ends once the motion it started has run, and each participant hears finished (see the End of cupertino_transaction_v1). Version 1 ended only a transaction bound to a gesture, so a participant of any other could not tell when it was over.

entry.name: serial
entry.summary: the connection already has a transaction of that serial that has not ended

entry.name: too_many
entry.summary: the connection takes part in 16 transactions that have not ended, or holds 256 holes

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface belongs to another client or is gone

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the surface is not a layer of cupertino_layers_v1, or already has a hole

entry.name: permission
entry.summary: the connection does not hold the role the request needs

entry.name: component
entry.summary: not a name of the server's component table

request.name: destroy

description.summary: unbind the global

request.description: Transactions and holes created through this global stay valid.

request.name: create

description.summary: start describing a transaction

request.description: Creates the transaction named by this connection's component, its instance number and serial, on the clock of output: the times of the transaction are presentation times of that output. The connection is its creator and its first participant. Posts the serial error while the connection has a transaction of that serial that has not ended, and too_many when it takes part in 16 transactions that have not ended.

request.name: join

description.summary: take part in another component's transaction

request.description:
Makes this connection a participant of the transaction that instance of component created with serial. What the participant stages and asks for joins that transaction as its own part. A joined transaction counts towards the 16 of the connection.
The name may arrive before the creator's create: a join that finds no such transaction waits for it, at most 100 milliseconds, and the participant may stage and submit meanwhile; when none came, the participant's part starts as a transaction of its own, on the clock of output. When the creator's transaction is there, its output is the transaction's and the output of this request is not read. A join to a transaction that has started is late (see cupertino_transaction_v1). The server remembers a transaction for 10 seconds after it ended: a join in that time applies the participant's part with every animation at its end. An instance number other than that of the component's running connection names a transaction of an earlier instance, which this rule covers when it ended within 10 seconds; otherwise the part starts as a transaction of its own at once.
Posts the component error for a name that is not a component's and too_many when the connection takes part in 16 transactions that have not ended.

request.name: get_hole

description.summary: draw a window in a layer

request.description: Makes a layer of this client (a surface with a cupertino_layer_v1 object) a hole: the server draws the hole's source in the layer's bounds, below the layer's own content and above its glass. Needs the windows role. Posts invalid_surface for a surface of another client, role for a surface that is not a layer or already has a hole, permission without the windows role, and too_many when the connection holds 256 holes.

interface.name: cupertino_transaction_v1

description.summary: one participant's part of a transaction

interface.description:
Each participant has an object of its own for the transaction. Through it the participant stages surfaces, brackets window changes and submits.
Staging. From stage on, the commits of the surface are not applied: the server keeps them, a later one added to the earlier ones in order, as a synchronized subsurface's state is kept. Everything a commit applies is kept with it: the buffer, the damage, the state of the surface's layers, presentation and holes that is double-buffered on it, and the cached state of its subsurfaces. The commits of the surface's layer surfaces are kept as well, a layer made while the surface is staged included: a layer's content, which otherwise applies on the layer surface's own commit without waiting for its parent (cupertino_layers_v1), applies with the part and not before. A surface is staged in one transaction at a time.
Kept commits and the client's pace. The frame callbacks of a kept commit are answered on the frame clock of the surface's output: with the next frame of that output, as for a commit that was shown, and no more than once for each frame, so a client that draws keeps the output's pace. A kept buffer that a later kept commit of the same surface replaces is released at once, so a client with two or three buffers goes on drawing. The presentation feedback of a kept commit follows the frame that first shows it, and is discarded for a commit that a later one replaced.
Window changes. Between begin_window_changes and end_window_changes, the requests this connection makes on its role objects that change windows are kept as well: activate_window, restore_window, activate_app, app_command, switch_workspace, move_workspace, add_workspace, remove_workspace, move_window, move_to_workspace, window_command and a window manager's commit with its placements. The server carries them out at the transaction's start, and the animations it runs for them (a window restored, raised or placed, a workspace switched) start there. Any other request is carried out when it arrives. The role requests are the connection's, so a connection has one open bracket at most, whichever of its transactions opened it.
Ready. A participant is ready when it has sent submit and each surface it staged has committed at least once since. A participant that has not sent submit 100 milliseconds after it created or joined is taken as having sent it. A part does not wait without end: 100 milliseconds after its submit, a participant with a staged surface that has not committed is ready as it stands. That surface leaves the part and commits as usual from then, and the rest of the part, the kept commits of its other surfaces and its window changes, is applied. In a transaction bound to a gesture (bind_gesture) the surface stays in the part: the transaction waits for its gesture anyway, and its first commit, however late, is kept for the gesture like the others.
Start. The transaction starts on the first frame of its output that the server prepares after its creator and every component the creator expects are ready, and at the latest on the first frame prepared after the deadline, counted from the creator's submit. A component that is stopped, lost, unresponsive or reported busy is not waited for. On that frame the server applies the kept commits of every ready participant and carries out their window changes. The start time is the presentation time of that frame. Every animation the transaction starts counts its time from the start time, on every output: an output shows the transaction on its first frame presented at or after the start time, with each animation as far along as that frame's own presentation time says. When the transaction's output is gone or shows no frame, the start time is the server's clock when the transaction became ready or the deadline passed.
Late. A participant that becomes ready after the start joins then: its kept commits are applied and its window changes carried out on the next frame, and each animation they start runs as if it had started at the start time, from the value and velocity its property had then, so it is as far along as the others; one whose end has passed is at its end. A late animation of a property that a transaction with a later start time animates is dropped: the later transaction keeps the property.
One property, two transactions. An animation started by a later transaction replaces the earlier one of the same property from the value and velocity shown at the later start, as cupertino_layer_v1 retargets, and its client hears replaced there. The earlier transaction goes on with its other animations.
End. The transaction ends when every participant that did not withdraw had its part applied, every animation its parts started has finished or been replaced, and the window changes have been carried out and the server's window motion they started (a window restored, placed or faded, the desktops sliding) has come to rest: the server applies the parts and runs every animation, so it is the one that knows. Each participant that still holds its object hears finished with completed, after the finished or replaced of each of its layer animations; one that destroyed its object after submit hears nothing, and its part still counts until the end. An ended transaction no longer counts towards the 16 of its connections. A transaction bound to a gesture ends where its progress comes to rest instead (bind_gesture).
Reduced motion. While reduce_motion is on, animations follow cupertino_layer_v1: those of the spatial properties are at their target in their first frame and opacity animates as asked, and the server's own window changes take their reduced form. The start, the deadline, the late rule and the end are the same: the end comes once the reduced motion has run, a fade at its end and a spatial change at its target at once.
A participant's connection ending. What the participant had kept and not applied is dropped, and the transaction does not wait for it. What had started ends with its surfaces: on a surface the server holds (cupertino_component_v1.persist) every animation is at its end at once and the holes and claims stay, and a transient surface is dismissed with its animations and holes. The other participants' parts are not touched. When the creator of a transaction bound to a gesture goes, the binding ends: a gesture under way is settled back to the start.

entry.name: creator
entry.summary: a request only the creator may make came from another participant

entry.name: submitted
entry.summary: stage, expect, set_deadline, bind_gesture, bind_reverse_gesture or begin_window_changes after submit

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface belongs to another client, is gone or has no role

entry.name: staged
entry.summary: the surface is staged in a transaction that has not started

entry.name: bracket
entry.summary: begin_window_changes while the connection has an open bracket, end_window_changes on an object that opened none, or submit inside one

entry.name: invalid_spring
entry.summary: a spring response outside 0.01 to 10 seconds or a damping ratio outside 0.05 to 4

entry.name: invalid_gesture
entry.summary: not an entry of gesture, or a reverse binding without a binding

entry.name: permission
entry.summary: the connection does not hold the role the request needs

entry.name: too_many
entry.summary: more than 32 staged surfaces or 16 expected components

entry.name: component
entry.summary: not a name of the server's component table

request.name: destroy

description.summary: let go of the transaction

request.description: Before the participant's submit this withdraws its part: its kept commits are applied at once, as ordinary commits, its kept window changes are carried out at once, an open bracket of this object is closed, and the transaction does not wait for it. After submit the part stays in the transaction and only the events end. Destroying the creator's object of a transaction bound to a gesture also ends its bindings: a gesture under way is settled back to the start.

request.name: expect

description.summary: wait for another component's part

request.description: The creator names a component whose part belongs at the start: the transaction waits for that component to join and be ready, until the deadline. Posts creator from another participant, component for a name that is not a component's and too_many for a 17th name.

request.name: set_deadline

description.summary: how long the start waits for the expected components

request.description: The longest time, counted from the creator's submit, that the start waits. Without this request it is one frame interval of the transaction's output plus 4 milliseconds. A deadline over 100 milliseconds is held at 100. Posts creator from another participant.

request.name: stage

description.summary: keep a surface's commits for the transaction

request.description: The surface is one with a role (a layer shell surface, a window or a popup), not a layer: a layer's state travels in its parent's commit, and the commits of the layers of a staged surface are kept with it. From this request until the participant's part is applied, the commits of the surface and of its layer surfaces are kept (see the interface). Posts invalid_surface, staged when the surface is staged in a transaction that has not started, and too_many for a 33rd surface.

request.name: begin_window_changes

description.summary: keep the window changes that follow

request.description: Opens the bracket: the window changes this connection asks for on its role objects from here to end_window_changes are kept for the transaction, in order. A role request that fails its own checks is refused when it arrives, as outside a bracket. Posts bracket while the connection has an open bracket, on this object or on another of its transactions.

request.name: end_window_changes

description.summary: close the bracket

request.description: Posts bracket when this object opened no bracket that is open.

entry.name: swipe_up
entry.summary: a three- or four-finger swipe up

entry.name: swipe_down
entry.summary: a three- or four-finger swipe down

entry.name: pinch
entry.summary: a four-finger pinch in

entry.name: spread
entry.summary: a four-finger spread

request.name: bind_gesture

description.summary: let a gesture drive the transaction

request.description:
The transaction does not start when it is ready: it waits, armed, for the gesture on its output. Needs the overview role; only the creator binds. While a transaction is armed for a gesture on an output, that gesture goes to it and is not reported to the dock.
A touchpad gesture belongs to one output: the output under the pointer at the moment the server's recogniser claims the gesture, until the fingers lift. One binding takes the gesture. When several wait for the same gesture on that output, the server picks at that moment: first a reverse binding (bind_reverse_gesture) of a transaction at rest completed, the one that completed last; then a binding of an armed transaction, the one armed last. The bindings passed over stay as they are and take a later gesture. A gesture under way is never handed from one binding to another.
When the recogniser claims the gesture, the transaction starts with the participants that are ready (gesture_began): their kept commits are applied and the values they set take effect, and every animation they start is tracked. A tracked animation shows its start value plus the gesture's progress times the way to its target, whatever its curve; an animation through samples shows the sample at that progress. The progress is the recogniser's, 0 where the gesture began and 1 for a whole gesture, held between the two.
When the fingers lift, the recogniser decides whether the gesture is completed or reverted (gesture_ended), and the server moves the progress to 1 or back to 0 along the spring of this request, starting from the gesture's velocity: response is the period of the undamped spring in seconds, damping its damping ratio. The window changes of the transaction are carried out when the progress comes to rest at 1, and dropped when it comes to rest at 0. At rest every participant hears finished.
A participant that becomes ready while the gesture is under way joins at the progress shown then. While reduce_motion is on, the progress drives opacity alone: a spatial property keeps its start value until the progress comes to rest at 1 and takes its target there.
An armed transaction keeps the commits of its staged surfaces until the gesture begins, so it suits a surface that shows nothing before; the participant stages again to describe another start. Posts creator, permission, invalid_gesture, invalid_spring, and submitted after submit.

request.name: bind_reverse_gesture

description.summary: let a second gesture drive the transaction back

request.description: Once the transaction has come to rest completed, this gesture on its output drives the same properties back: its progress runs from 1 towards 0, between the values they show at rest and the values they had when the first gesture began, and the release settles along the same spring. Reverted, the transaction is over and its bindings end; completed again, the reverse gesture stays armed. Window changes are not undone. The binding lasts until the creator destroys its object or cancels. While the transaction rests completed, this binding comes before the binding of any armed transaction for the same gesture on the output (see bind_gesture). Posts invalid_gesture without a bind_gesture before it, and the errors of bind_gesture.

request.name: submit

description.summary: the participant's part is described

request.description: Nothing more is staged or bracketed for this participant. Posts bracket inside an open bracket.

request.name: cancel

description.summary: give the transaction up

request.description: From a participant that is not the creator, cancel is destroy without the object going away. From the creator it ends the transaction for everyone. Before the start, every participant's kept commits are applied at once as ordinary commits and its kept window changes carried out at once, each part by itself: a participant that wants its change undone commits the opposite before it cancels. After the start, every animation the transaction started stops at the value shown on the next frame, and its client hears replaced with that value; window changes that were carried out stay. An armed transaction is disarmed as before the start; one whose gesture is under way is settled back to its start. Every participant hears finished with cancelled, and the transaction ends.

event.name: started

description.summary: the transaction started

event.description: Sent to each participant when its part is applied: the start time, as the presentation clock gives it (the clock of wp_presentation), which is the time every animation of the transaction counts from. A late participant gets the original start time. Not sent for a transaction bound to a gesture, which sends gesture_began.

event.name: gesture_began

description.summary: the bound gesture drives the transaction

event.description: Sent to each participant: the gesture of bind_gesture, or of bind_reverse_gesture, began on the transaction's output. A participant that has not staged its part does so on this event and joins at the progress shown.

entry.name: completed
entry.summary: at its end: every change reached its target

entry.name: reverted
entry.summary: a gesture took it back to its start

entry.name: cancelled
entry.summary: the creator cancelled it

event.name: gesture_ended

description.summary: the fingers lifted

event.description: The transaction settles towards outcome, completed or reverted, along the binding's spring; finished follows when it is at rest.

event.name: finished

description.summary: the transaction is at rest

event.description: Sent to each participant when the transaction ended: one no gesture drives once its motion has run (see End), with completed, or when it is cancelled; one bound to a gesture each time it comes to rest. After completed with a reverse binding the transaction stays, for that gesture; after reverted or cancelled it is over. A join to a transaction that ended hears it at once.

interface.name: cupertino_hole_v1

description.summary: a layer in which the server draws a window

interface.description:
The hole fills its layer's bounds as the layer is shown and moves, scales, fades and is clipped with it; the layer's animations are the hole's. Its source is drawn to fit the bounds with its proportions kept, centred. The pixels are the server's: the component never receives them, and a capture of the screen leaves out of a hole whatever it leaves out of the source's own place.
The state of a hole is double-buffered with its layer's: it applies on the commit of the layer's parent, and a staged parent carries it into the transaction. A hole takes no input: pointer and touch go to the parent surface, and the component decides what a press on the hole means.
A hole of a surface the server holds (cupertino_component_v1.persist) stays with it: it goes on drawing its source and keeps its claim until a surface takes the hold over or the hold ends.

entry.name: invalid_source
entry.summary: not an entry of source

entry.name: permission
entry.summary: the connection does not hold the role the request needs

entry.name: none
entry.summary: nothing is drawn

entry.name: window
entry.summary: a window as it shows, with its decorations and its shadow, live

entry.name: thumbnail
entry.summary: a minimized window as it last showed, without its shadow

entry.name: workspace
entry.summary: a workspace as it is: its wallpaper and its windows, live

request.name: destroy

description.summary: remove the hole

request.description: The hole goes with the next commit of its layer's parent, and its claim with it.

request.name: set_source

description.summary: what the hole shows

request.description: id is a window id, the same as the feeds of the role objects give, or a workspace id. An id that names nothing draws nothing: the window may have just closed. The workspace source needs the overview role. Posts invalid_source and permission.

request.name: set_claim

description.summary: take the window off its own place

request.description:
1 claims the window of a window source: from the commit that applies it the window is drawn in this hole alone, not at its own frame, and takes no pointer or touch input. 0, the initial state, leaves the window where it is. A hole that sets the claim in the commit that first shows it, with its layer where the window shows, takes the window over without a change on screen. Needs the overview or the window manager role.
The claims of a window stack in the order their commits applied them. The latest is in force: the window is drawn in its hole. Every claim below it is suspended, and its hole draws nothing meanwhile. When the claim in force ends, the one below it is in force again and the window is drawn in that hole; when none is left, the window is at its own frame. So where a window shows without a claim is the hole of the claim below it, or its own frame. The overview's claim over the stage strip's is such a stack.
When a claim ends with a commit of the component (set_claim 0, or the hole or its layer destroyed), the window is drawn where it shows without that claim from that commit. When it ends any other way (the surface is dismissed, the connection ends and the surface is not held), the server moves the window there from where the hole showed it along its return motion, so no window jumps. A suspended claim that ends changes nothing on screen.
Posts permission without one of the roles.

event.name: source_closed

description.summary: the hole's window or workspace is gone

event.description: The window closed, or the workspace was removed. A window source keeps the window's last picture and fades it out where the hole lies, along the server's closing animation; after that, and for a workspace at once, the hole draws nothing. A thumbnail source is also closed when its window stops being minimized. The component lays its surface out again without the hole.
